html: The Coharie are a Native American people of Sampson and Harnett counties in south-eastern North Carolina, named for the Great Coharie and Little Coharie creeks. They are believed to descend from peoples of the Carolina coastal plain who took refuge inland in the 1700s. Under segregation they ran their own schools, among them the East Carolina Indian School, from the 1940s to the 1960s. North Carolina recognised the Coharie Intra-Tribal Council in 1971; they are not recognised by the federal government. Nearby peoples include the Lumbee and the Waccamaw Siouan, and the Tuscarora once held land to the north.
